title: How can three angles of a quadrilateral give the fourth?
description: Three angles of a four sided shape are seventy five, ninety five and one hundred ten degrees. The video cuts the shape into two triangles to get the total of the four angles, and Keeko then doubts and says the fourth angle is ninety degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal cuts a four sided shape into two triangles, so its four angles add to three hundred sixty degrees. Watch for students who guess ninety for the fourth angle because rectangles have right angles.

source: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 95° and 110°. Find the fourth angle.
video_script.why: The child sees why the four angles of any quadrilateral add to three hundred sixty degrees, and uses the total to find the fourth angle when three are known.
video_script.substitution: Cut the shape into two triangles with a diagonal, add the angles of the two triangles, and take the three known angles away from the total.
video_script.anchor: a four sided shape with a diagonal, three angles marked 75, 95 and 110 degrees and the fourth angle unknown
video_script.wrong_answer: the fourth angle is ninety degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the fourth angle is ninety degrees, like the corner of a rectangle; but nothing makes this corner square, and the four angles would then add to 370 degrees instead of 360.
video_script.payoff_line: The fourth angle is eighty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the fourth angle is eighty degrees

maths_rules: a diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, each with angle sum 180 degrees
the angles of the two triangles together make the four angles of the quadrilateral, so the total is 180 + 180 = 360 degrees
check: with 90 the total would be 280 + 90 = 370, which is not 360
video_script.design: One idea: two triangles give a total of 360 degrees, and the fourth angle is what is left. Wrong idea: the fourth angle is 90 degrees. The shape with its diagonal stays on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the fourth angle is ninety degrees, like the corner of a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>But nothing in this shape makes the corner square. With ninety, the four angles would add to three hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is more than three hundred sixty, so ninety cannot be right.
